newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee retail prices fell 10 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: German coffee retail prices fell 10 pct in 1996.

text.p: Average retail coffee prices in Germany declined by 10 percent in 1996 to 6.80 marks per 0.5 kg of roasted coffee, the DKV coffee industry association said.
A year-end statement from the DKV said short-term price rises were out of the question as fierce competition in the retailing and wholesaling sectors prevented this.
Coffee as a quality product was undervalued. A tax of 2.15 marks per 0.5 kg is included in the price.
Roasters' profits were under pressure from lower operating margins but they were also worried by flat consumption, the DKV said.
Young people in particular were turning to cold soft drinks instead of coffee, unlike other markets such as the U.S. where coffee was a fashionable "lifestyle" product.
The DKV would launch publicity campaigns to counter this trend.
German coffee consumption was likely to have fallen in 1996, the DKV said, but it gave no figures.
Forecasts up to now have put green coffee equivalent consumption at the 564,000 tonnes seen in 1995.
Looking at raw materials trends, DKV noted falling stocks of green coffee, which brought higher physical differentials over futures for spot coffees of good quality.
German roasters' buying-in prices were 15 percent up from a year ago, also due to the firmer dollar, DKV said.
